creation-light: Before there was anything — no sun, no earth, no time — there was God.
The world was dark, empty and shapeless.
Then God spoke one sentence: “Let there be light.”
And light appeared. Over six days He made the sky, land, seas, plants, stars, animals, and finally people, and He called it all very good.
creation-eve: God made Adam and put him in a beautiful garden, but said, “It isn’t good for him to be alone.”
So God put Adam into a deep sleep, took part of his side, and made a woman.
When Adam woke up and saw her, he was overjoyed: “At last — she is part of me!”
This was the very first marriage.
eden: Adam and Eve could eat from any tree in the garden except one.
A crafty serpent convinced Eve that God was keeping something good from them.
She ate the fruit and gave some to Adam.
Right away they felt ashamed and hid.
God sent them out of the garden and placed angels with a flaming sword at the gate.
cain-abel: Adam and Eve’s sons both brought gifts to God.
God accepted Abel’s gift but not Cain’s, and Cain became furious and jealous.
God warned him to control his anger, but Cain lured his brother into a field and killed him.
When God asked where Abel was, Cain shrugged: “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
flood: The world had become so violent that God decided to start over.
He told Noah, the one good man left, to build a giant boat.
Noah, his family and the animals went inside, and it rained for 40 days and nights.
The water rose over the highest mountains, and the ark floated on top of it all.
dove: After months on the water, the rain stopped and the flood slowly went down.
Noah sent out a dove to see if there was dry land.
The first time it came back with nothing.
The second time, it came back in the evening with a fresh olive leaf in its beak.
Noah knew the worst was over.
babel: After the flood, people all spoke one language.
They decided to build a city with a tower reaching the sky — to make a name for themselves.
God came down to see it, and He mixed up their language so they couldn’t understand each other.
They stopped building and spread out across the world.
three-angels: Abraham was sitting at his tent door in the heat of the day when three strangers appeared.
He ran to greet them, bowed, and threw together a big meal.
It turned out the Lord Himself was visiting.
He told Abraham that by this time next year, his old wife Sarah would finally have a son.
sodom: The cities of Sodom and Gomorrah were so wicked that God decided to destroy them.
Two angels pulled Abraham’s nephew Lot and his family out and warned them: “Run for your lives — and don’t look back!”
Fire and burning sulfur rained down.
But Lot’s wife looked back and turned into a pillar of salt.
hagar: Abraham sent away Hagar, Sarah’s servant, and her son Ishmael with just some bread and water.
When the water ran out in the desert, Hagar put the boy under a bush and walked away so she wouldn’t have to watch him die.
Then an angel called to her: God had heard the boy crying.
He showed her a well, and they lived.
jacob-dream: Jacob was running from his brother Esau, whom he’d tricked.
That night he slept outside with a rock for a pillow.
He dreamed of a stairway reaching to heaven, with angels going up and down.
At the top stood the Lord, who promised to protect him and bless the whole world through his family.
Jacob woke up and said, “God was here and I didn’t even know it.”
jacob-wrestles: The night before Jacob had to face Esau, he was alone by a river when a mysterious man wrestled with him until dawn.
The man injured Jacob’s hip, but Jacob held on: “I won’t let go until you bless me.”
The man gave him a new name — Israel, “he struggles with God.”
Jacob realized he had seen God face to face.
jacob-esau: Twenty years after Jacob stole his brother’s blessing, he finally had to face Esau, who was coming with 400 men.
Jacob was terrified and bowed to the ground seven times.
But Esau ran to him, threw his arms around him, kissed him, and they both cried.
joseph-sold: Joseph was his father’s favorite son, and his brothers hated him for it.
When he came to check on them in the fields, they threw him into an empty well.
Then they saw some traders heading to Egypt and sold Joseph to them for 20 pieces of silver.
They dipped his special coat in goat blood and told their father a wild animal had killed him.
joseph-reveals: Years later, Joseph was the second most powerful man in Egypt.
A famine brought his brothers to Egypt to buy food, and they bowed before him without recognizing him.
After testing them, Joseph couldn’t hold back.
He sent everyone out, started crying so loudly the whole palace heard, and said: “I am Joseph — the brother you sold.”
moses-nile: Pharaoh had ordered every Hebrew baby boy thrown into the Nile.
One mother hid her baby for three months.
When she couldn’t hide him any longer, she made a little basket waterproofed with tar, put him inside, and set it among the reeds at the river’s edge.
His big sister watched from a distance to see what would happen.
moses-found: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to the river to bathe and spotted the basket in the reeds.
She opened it, saw the crying baby boy, and felt sorry for him.
His big sister stepped up and offered to find a nurse — and brought the baby’s own mother.
Pharaoh’s daughter adopted him and named him Moses.
let-my-people-go: After God spoke to him from a burning bush, Moses and his brother Aaron walked into the palace of the most powerful king on earth.
They gave him God’s message: “Let my people go.”
I don’t know Him, and I won’t let Israel go.”
Instead, he made the slaves work even harder.
darkness: Pharaoh kept refusing to free the Israelites, so God sent plague after plague.
The ninth was darkness — so thick you could almost feel it.
For three days nobody in Egypt could see anyone or even leave their house.
But in the homes where the Israelites lived, there was light.
passover: God warned that the last plague would be the worst: at midnight every firstborn son in Egypt would die.
The Israelites were told to put lamb’s blood on their doorframes so death would “pass over” their homes.
At midnight it happened, and loud crying filled Egypt.
Pharaoh finally told the Israelites to go.
Jews still remember this night at Passover.
red-sea: Pharaoh changed his mind and chased the Israelites with his army, trapping them against the sea.
Moses raised his staff, and God split the water so they walked across on dry ground.
When the Egyptians followed, Moses raised his hand again and the sea crashed back over the army.
sinai: Three months after leaving Egypt, the Israelites camped at the foot of Mount Sinai.
On the third day there was thunder, lightning and a thick cloud.
The whole mountain shook and was covered in smoke, because God had come down on it in fire.
A trumpet blast grew louder and louder.
Then God spoke the Ten Commandments.
tablets: Moses spent 40 days on the mountain with God, receiving the law written on two stone tablets.
Meanwhile the people got impatient and had Aaron make a golden calf, which they worshiped and partied around.
When Moses came down and saw it, he was so angry he threw the tablets to the ground and smashed them.
serpent: In the desert, the Israelites complained against God again, and poisonous snakes came into the camp.
Many people were bitten and died.
When they admitted they were wrong, God told Moses to make a bronze snake and put it on a pole.
Anyone who was bitten could look at it and live.
Jesus later compared Himself to that snake on a pole.
balaam: A king paid a prophet named Balaam to curse Israel.
On the way, Balaam’s donkey kept swerving off the road, and Balaam beat her.
Finally God opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw what the donkey had seen all along — an angel standing in the road with a drawn sword.
Balaam ended up blessing Israel instead.
jordan: After 40 years in the desert, Israel finally reached the Jordan River — at flood stage.
God told the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant to step into the water.
The moment their feet touched it, the river stopped flowing and piled up upstream.
The whole nation walked across on dry ground into the Promised Land.
jericho: Jericho had huge walls and locked gates.
God gave Joshua a strange battle plan: march around the city once a day for six days in silence.
On the seventh day, march around seven times, then the priests blow their trumpets and everyone shouts.
They did exactly that — and the walls fell down flat.
sun-stands: Five kings attacked Israel’s allies, and Joshua marched all night to defend them.
As the battle raged, Joshua prayed a bold prayer in front of everyone: “Sun, stand still!”
And the Bible says the sun stopped in the middle of the sky for about a whole day until Israel won.
There was never a day like it.
gideon: Gideon gathered 32,000 men to fight the Midianites.
God said, “Too many — you’ll think you won on your own.”
First the scared ones went home.
Then God had the rest drink from a stream and kept only the 300 who lapped water from their hands.
With jars, torches and trumpets, those 300 sent the whole enemy army running.
samson-lion: Samson was walking through the vineyards near a town called Timnah when a young lion came roaring at him.
The Spirit of the Lord came over him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as easily as you’d tear a young goat.
He didn’t even tell his parents what he had done.
delilah: The Philistine leaders each offered Delilah a fortune to find out what made Samson so strong.
She kept nagging him until he finally told her the truth: his hair had never been cut.
While he slept with his head in her lap, she had a man shave it off.
His strength was gone, and the Philistines captured him.
samson-death: The Philistines blinded Samson, chained him, and made him grind grain in prison.
At a huge party to celebrate, they brought him out to mock him.
Samson asked the boy leading him to put his hands on the two main pillars.
He prayed, “Lord, remember me — give me strength one more time.”
He pushed, and the building collapsed on everyone inside.
ruth-naomi: Naomi lost her husband and both her sons in a foreign land and decided to go home to Bethlehem.
She told her two daughters-in-law to go back to their own families.
One left, but Ruth refused: “Don’t ask me to leave you.
Where you go, I will go.
Your people will be my people, and your God my God.”
ruth-boaz: To feed herself and Naomi, Ruth went to pick up leftover grain in the fields.
The owner, a kind man named Boaz, noticed her and told his workers to leave extra for her.
Ruth bowed and asked why he was so kind to a foreigner.
Boaz said he’d heard everything she did for Naomi — and he blessed her. Later they married.
goliath: For 40 days the giant Goliath dared Israel’s army to fight him, and everyone was afraid.
Young David, there to bring food to his brothers, volunteered.
He refused the king’s armor and took his sling and five stones.
He told Goliath, “You come with a sword, but I come in the name of the Lord.”
One stone hit Goliath in the forehead, and the giant fell.
jonathan: After David beat Goliath, King Saul’s son Jonathan became his best friend.
The Bible says Jonathan loved David as much as his own life.
He gave David his robe, sword and bow, and they made a promise of friendship.
Later, Jonathan even protected David from his own father.
spares-saul: King Saul was hunting David to kill him.
Saul went into a cave to relieve himself — the very cave where David and his men were hiding.
David’s men whispered, “This is your chance!”
David crept up and quietly cut off a corner of Saul’s robe instead.
Then he called out to Saul and showed him: I could have killed you, but I won’t harm God’s chosen king.
absalom: David’s son Absalom tried to steal the throne and went to war against his own father.
In the battle, Absalom’s long hair got caught in a tree, and David’s general killed him.
When David heard the news, he went up to a room and wept: “My son Absalom!
If only I had died instead of you!”
solomon-judgment: Two women came to King Solomon, both claiming the same baby was theirs.
Solomon called for a sword and said, “Cut the baby in two and give each one half.”
Give her the baby — just don’t kill him!”
sheba: The Queen of Sheba heard how wise Solomon was and traveled a long way with camels loaded with gold, spices and jewels to test him with hard questions.
When she saw his wisdom and everything he’d built, she was breathless: “What I heard wasn’t even half of it.”
widows-son: During a drought, Elijah stayed with a poor widow whose flour and oil miraculously never ran out.
Then her son got sick and died.
Elijah carried the boy upstairs, stretched himself over him three times, and cried out to God.
Elijah carried him down and said, “Look — your son is alive.”
carmel: Elijah challenged 450 prophets of Baal: each side builds an altar, and the god who sends fire is the true God.
Baal’s prophets shouted and danced all day — nothing.
Elijah had his altar soaked with water three times, then prayed one simple prayer.
Fire fell from heaven and burned up everything, even the water.
The people fell down and shouted, “The Lord is God!”
elijah-angel: Right after his big victory, Queen Jezebel threatened to kill Elijah.
He ran into the desert, sat under a tree and asked God to let him die.
He fell asleep. An angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
There was warm bread and water.
He ate, slept again, and the angel fed him again: “The journey is too much for you.”
chariot: Elijah knew God was about to take him.
His apprentice Elisha refused to leave his side.
As they walked and talked, a chariot of fire with horses of fire suddenly came between them, and Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elisha picked up Elijah’s fallen cloak and carried on his work.
sennacherib: The huge Assyrian army surrounded Jerusalem, and their king sent a letter mocking God.
King Hezekiah took the letter into the Temple, spread it out before God, and prayed.
That very night the angel of the Lord went through the Assyrian camp, and by morning 185,000 soldiers were dead.
ezra: Ezra, a priest, came back to Jerusalem from exile and learned that the people had already fallen back into the same sins that got them exiled.
He was so heartbroken he tore his clothes and sat stunned until evening.
Then he fell on his knees, spread out his hands, and prayed: “My God, I’m too ashamed to even look up.”
nehemiah: Nehemiah worked for the king of Persia when he heard Jerusalem’s walls were still in ruins.
He got permission to go, inspected the broken walls secretly at night, and then told the people: “Come, let’s rebuild the wall.”
Despite threats and mockery, they finished it in just 52 days.
esther: Haman’s plot meant every Jew in Persia would be killed.
Queen Esther could stop it — but walking in to see the king without being called could get her executed.
After three days of fasting, she put on her royal robes and stood in the court.
The king saw her and held out his golden scepter: she could live, and speak.
job: In one terrible day, messengers came one after another to tell Job he had lost his oxen, his sheep, his camels, his servants — and then all ten of his children, killed when a house collapsed.
Job tore his robe, shaved his head, and fell to the ground.
But he worshiped: “The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away.
Blessed be the name of the Lord.”
isaiah: Isaiah had a vision of God on a high throne, with angels calling out “Holy, holy, holy.”
An angel touched his lips with a hot coal and said, “Your guilt is gone.”
Then God asked, “Who will go for us?”
He said, “Here I am. Send me.”
leviathan: Leviathan was an ancient name for a terrifying sea monster — a symbol of chaos and evil.
Isaiah promised that one day God will take His great, strong sword and destroy it once and for all.
It’s a picture of God finally defeating everything that is evil and frightening in the world.
jeremiah: When Jeremiah was young, God spoke to him: “Before I formed you in your mother’s womb, I knew you.
Before you were born, I set you apart.”
Jeremiah protested that he was too young and didn’t know how to speak.
God touched his mouth and said, “I have put my words in your mouth.”
ezekiel: Ezekiel spoke to the Jews in exile in Babylon, people who felt hopeless and far from God.
God gave him a promise for them: “I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you.
I will take out your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.”
furnace: King Nebuchadnezzar ordered everyone to bow to his giant gold statue or be thrown into a blazing furnace.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refused: “Our God can save us — but even if He doesn’t, we still won’t bow.”
The furious king threw them in.
Then he saw four men walking around in the fire, unhurt.
writing-wall: King Belshazzar threw a wild party and drank from the holy cups stolen from God’s Temple.
Suddenly human fingers appeared and wrote on the palace wall.
The king turned pale and his knees knocked.
Daniel was called in and read it: God has numbered your days, you’ve been weighed and found lacking, and your kingdom will be given away.
That night the king was killed.
lions-den: Jealous officials tricked the king into making a law: pray to anyone but the king and you’ll be thrown to the lions.
Daniel kept praying to God three times a day by his open window.
The king, who liked Daniel, was heartbroken but had to throw him in.
At dawn the king ran to the den.
Daniel called out: “My God sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths.”
jonah-whale: Jonah ran from God on a ship, a huge storm hit, and the sailors threw him overboard.
God sent a great fish to swallow him.
For three days and nights Jonah sat in the dark inside the fish, and he prayed.
Then God spoke to the fish, and it spit Jonah out onto dry land.
nineveh: Jonah finally went to Nineveh and walked through the city shouting, “In 40 days Nineveh will be destroyed!”
To everyone’s surprise, the whole city believed God.
The king took off his royal robes, sat in ashes and told everyone to turn from evil.
When God saw them change, He had mercy and didn’t destroy them.
annunciation: In the town of Nazareth, the angel Gabriel appeared to a young woman named Mary.
He told her not to be afraid — God was pleased with her.
She would have a baby boy and name him Jesus.
He would be called the Son of the Most High, and His kingdom would never end.
Mary answered: “I am the Lord’s servant. Let it happen.”
nativity: Mary and Joseph had to travel to Bethlehem for a Roman census.
When they got there, there was no room for them in the guest room.
Mary gave birth to Jesus, wrapped Him in cloth, and laid Him in a manger — a feeding trough for animals.
That night angels told shepherds in the fields the good news.
temple-boy: When Jesus was 12, His family went to Jerusalem for Passover.
On the way home, Mary and Joseph realized He wasn’t with them.
After three days of searching, they found Him in the Temple, sitting with the teachers, listening and asking questions.
Everyone was amazed at how much He understood.
He said, “Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?”
baptist: John the Baptist lived in the desert, wore clothes made of camel hair and ate locusts and wild honey.
Crowds came out from Jerusalem to hear him preach: “Turn back to God — the kingdom of heaven is near!”
People confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
He said someone much greater was coming after him.
baptism: Jesus came to the Jordan River and asked John to baptize Him.
John said, “I should be baptized by you!” but Jesus insisted.
As Jesus came up out of the water, the sky opened, the Spirit of God came down on Him like a dove, and a voice from heaven said: “This is my Son, whom I love.
I am very pleased with Him.”
cana: Jesus and His disciples were at a wedding when the wine ran out — a huge embarrassment for the family.
Mary told the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”
Jesus had them fill six big stone jars with water and take some to the person in charge.
He tasted it — it was wine, and better than anything they had served all night.
fishers: Peter and his partners had fished all night and caught nothing.
Jesus told Peter to go out again and drop the nets.
Peter said, “We’ve worked all night… but because you say so, I will.”
They caught so many fish the nets started breaking and two boats nearly sank.
Jesus said, “From now on you’ll fish for people.”
sermon: When Jesus saw the crowds, He went up on a hillside and sat down to teach.
He turned everything upside down: the poor in spirit, the grieving, the humble and the merciful are the truly blessed ones.
He taught people to love their enemies, to pray the Lord’s Prayer, and to build their lives on His words like a house on rock.
samaritan-woman: Jesus sat by a well at noon and asked a Samaritan woman for a drink — something Jewish men didn’t do.
He told her that if she drank water from the well, she’d be thirsty again, but the water He gives becomes a spring inside you that never runs dry.
He knew everything about her past, and she ran to tell the whole town.
tempest: Jesus and His disciples were crossing the lake in a boat when a violent storm hit.
Jesus was asleep on a cushion.
The terrified disciples woke Him: “Don’t you care that we’re about to die?”
Jesus stood up, told the wind and waves, “Quiet!
Be still!” — and everything went completely calm.
walks-on-water: John the Baptist was Jesus' cousin and the man who announced him to the world.
Now John was dead.
King Herod had him killed, and John's followers came and told Jesus.
Jesus wanted to be alone, so he took a boat across the Sea of Galilee to a quiet place.
But the crowds saw him leave.
They ran along the shore and got there first.
Jesus looked at thousands of people and felt sorry for them.
He healed their sick all day.
When evening came, the disciples said, send them away to buy food.
Jesus said, you give them something to eat.
All they had was five loaves of bread and two fish.
Jesus thanked God for it, broke it, and handed it out.
About five thousand men ate, plus women and children, and twelve baskets of leftovers were picked up.
The crowd was so amazed that they wanted to take Jesus and make him king by force.
John's gospel tells us this.
So Jesus did something unexpected.
He made his disciples get in the boat and go ahead of him to the other side.
He sent the crowd home.
Then he climbed a mountain alone to pray.
Out on the lake, the disciples were in trouble.
A strong wind was blowing against them, and the waves were pounding the boat.
They had been rowing for hours.
John's gospel says they were only three or four miles from shore, but they couldn't get there.
Sometime between three and six in the morning, they were exhausted and afraid.
Then they saw someone walking toward them on the water.
They screamed. They thought it was a ghost.
Jesus called out, take courage.
It is I. Don't be afraid.
Peter was the bold, loud one of the twelve, a fisherman who had left his nets to follow Jesus.
He called back, Lord, if it's really you, tell me to come to you on the water.
Jesus said one word.
Come.
Peter climbed over the side and walked on the water toward Jesus.
Then he noticed the wind.
He got scared and started to sink.
He shouted, Lord, save me.
Jesus reached out and caught him right away.
He said, you of little faith, why did you doubt?
They climbed into the boat, and the wind stopped.
The disciples fell down and worshiped him.
They said, truly you are the Son of God.
In Matthew's gospel, this is the first time the disciples say that out loud.
Why does this matter?
In the Old Testament, only God walks on the sea.
Job says God alone treads on the waves.
And when Jesus says, it is I, those words can also be translated, I am.
That is the name God gave Moses at the burning bush.
This scene shows that Jesus is more than a teacher, and that he saves people who are sinking.
Peter's story didn't end in the water.
Later he would say out loud that Jesus is the Messiah, and Jesus would make him a leader of his followers.
Peter would also fail badly the night Jesus was arrested, and Jesus would reach for him again.
The boat reached the shore at Gennesaret, and people brought all their sick.
Everyone who touched Jesus' cloak was healed.
The next day, Jesus told the crowd that he is the bread of life.
What does this mean for us today?
Everyone ends up in a storm sometime.
It might be a sickness, a lost job, a broken family, or a fear that won't leave.
This story shows where Jesus is while it happens.
He came to the disciples in the middle of the storm.
He didn't wait for it to be over.
It also shows what faith looks like.
Peter didn't walk on the water because he was strong.
He walked because Jesus said, come.
He sank when he looked at the wind instead of at Jesus.
And when he sank, he did the only thing he could do.
He asked for help.
Lord, save me. Jesus caught him right away, with his hand already stretched out.
That is why this story is so important.
It shows that Jesus is God, with power over everything that scares us.
It shows that doubt doesn't disqualify anyone, because Peter doubted and was still caught, still called, and still became a leader.
And it shows that the right prayer in a storm can be three words.
Lord, save me.
multitude: More than 5,000 people had followed Jesus to a remote place, and it was getting late.
All the disciples could find was five small loaves and two fish.
Jesus had everyone sit on the grass, looked up to heaven, thanked God, and broke the bread.
Everyone ate until they were full — and the leftovers filled twelve baskets.
jairus: Jairus, a synagogue leader, begged Jesus to come heal his dying 12-year-old daughter.
Before they got there, messengers said she had died.
Jesus said, “Don’t be afraid — just believe.”
He went in, took the girl’s hand and said, “Little girl, get up.”
She got up and walked around, and Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
magdalene: Jesus was at dinner at a religious leader’s house when a woman known for her sinful life came in, cried at Jesus’ feet, wiped them with her hair, and poured perfume on them.
Jesus told him: her many sins are forgiven — that’s why she loves so much.
Then He told her, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
adulteress: The religious leaders dragged in a woman caught in adultery and asked Jesus whether she should be stoned, as the law said.
Jesus bent down and wrote in the dirt, then said: “Whoever has never sinned can throw the first stone.”
One by one, from oldest to youngest, they walked away.
Jesus told her, “I don’t condemn you either.
martha: Jesus came to visit Martha and her sister Mary.
Martha rushed around getting dinner ready while Mary just sat at Jesus’ feet listening.
Martha finally said, “Lord, don’t you care she’s left me to do all the work?”
Jesus said, “Martha, Martha, you’re worried about so many things.
Only one thing really matters — and Mary has chosen it.”
transfiguration: Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain.
There, right in front of them, He changed — His face shone like the sun and His clothes became bright white.
Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Him.
A cloud covered them, and God’s voice said, “This is my Son.
Listen to Him.” The disciples fell on their faces, terrified.
prodigal-decides: In a story Jesus told, a young man asked his father for his inheritance early, then ran off and wasted every penny on wild living.
When famine hit, he ended up feeding pigs and was so hungry he wanted to eat their food.
Finally he came to his senses: “My father’s servants have more than enough.
I’ll go home and ask to be a servant.”
prodigal-return: The son headed home, practicing his apology.
But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him, felt huge compassion, and ran to him — hugging and kissing him before he could finish his speech.
The father called for the best robe, a ring and a party: “My son was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found!”
rich-man: Jesus told about a rich man who dressed in luxury clothes and feasted every day, while a poor, sick beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, hoping for scraps.
Both men died. Lazarus was carried by angels to Abraham’s side, while the rich man was in torment — and now there was a great gap no one could cross.
publican: Jesus told about two men who went to pray.
One, a proud religious leader, stood up and thanked God he wasn’t like other sinners.
The other, a tax collector, stood far away, wouldn’t even look up, beat his chest and said, “God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
Jesus said the tax collector was the one who went home right with God.
palm-sunday: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey, just as an old prophecy said the King would.
Huge crowds spread their coats and palm branches on the road in front of Him and shouted, “Hosanna to the Son of David!
Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
The whole city was stirred up asking, “Who is this?”
tribute: Religious leaders tried to trap Jesus: “Should we pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
If He said yes, the people would hate Him; if no, Rome would arrest Him.
Jesus asked for a coin and asked whose picture was on it.
“Caesar’s.” Jesus said: “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar — and give God what belongs to God.” They were stunned.
last-supper: On the night before He died, Jesus ate the Passover meal with His disciples.
He took bread, thanked God, broke it and gave it to them: “This is my body, given for you.
After supper He took the cup: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.”
Christians still do this today in Communion.
gethsemane: After the Last Supper, Jesus went to a garden called Gethsemane to pray.
He knew what was coming and was so overwhelmed that His sweat was like drops of blood.
He prayed, “Father, if you’re willing, take this cup of suffering away from me.
But not my will — yours be done.”
judas-kiss: While Jesus was still talking in the garden, a crowd with swords and clubs showed up, led by Judas, one of the twelve.
Judas had told them, “The one I kiss is the man you want.”
He walked up and kissed Jesus.
Jesus said, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
peter-denies: Peter followed Jesus to the high priest’s courtyard and waited by a fire.
Three different times, people said he was one of Jesus’ followers, and three times Peter said, “I don’t know Him!”
As he spoke the third time, a rooster crowed.
Jesus turned and looked straight at Peter.
Peter remembered Jesus’ warning, went outside and cried bitterly.
thorns: After Pilate had Jesus whipped, the Roman soldiers decided to have some fun with the “King of the Jews.”
They twisted thorny branches into a crown and pushed it onto His head, threw a purple robe on Him like a king, and mocked Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!” — and hit Him in the face.
ecce-homo: Pilate brought Jesus out to the crowd, beaten and bleeding, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe.
Maybe he hoped they would feel sorry for Him.
He said, “Look — here is the man!”
But the chief priests and guards shouted back, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
calvary: Jesus was led outside Jerusalem to a hill called the Skull — Golgotha, or Calvary.
There the soldiers nailed Him to a cross.
Two criminals were crucified with Him, one on His right and one on His left.
A sign above His head said: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
nailed: As the soldiers nailed Him to the cross and gambled for His clothes, Jesus prayed — not for Himself, but for them: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
Even while dying, He was forgiving.
darkness-cross: From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
In the Temple, the huge curtain separating people from God’s presence tore in two.
Then Jesus cried out loudly, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit,” and He breathed His last.
A Roman officer watching said, “Surely this man was innocent.”
dead-christ: A rich council member named Joseph of Arimathea went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
He took it down from the cross, wrapped it in clean linen cloth, and laid it in a brand-new tomb cut into rock, where no one had ever been buried.
A big stone was rolled across the entrance.
It was Friday evening. Sunday was coming.
ascension: For 40 days after He rose from the dead, Jesus appeared to His followers.
Then on a hill near Jerusalem He blessed them and was taken up into the sky, and a cloud hid Him.
As they stared upward, two men in white appeared and said, “Why are you standing here looking at the sky?
Jesus will come back the same way you saw Him go.”
stephen: Stephen told the religious council that they had killed the Messiah.
They were so furious they covered their ears, dragged him outside the city and threw stones at him.
As he was dying, Stephen prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit,” then fell to his knees: “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them.”
A young man named Saul stood watching their coats.
cornelius: Cornelius was a Roman army officer — not Jewish — who prayed to God.
An angel told him to send for Peter.
Meanwhile God showed Peter a vision teaching him not to call anyone unclean.
When Peter arrived and heard Cornelius’s story, he said, “Now I really understand that God doesn’t play favorites.”
The Holy Spirit came on all the non-Jews listening.
peter-escape: King Herod threw Peter in prison, chained between two soldiers, planning to execute him the next day.
Suddenly an angel appeared, a light filled the cell, and the angel tapped Peter: “Get up, quick!”
The chains fell off his wrists.
Peter walked out past the guards, and the iron gate opened by itself.
paul-prison: In the city of Philippi, Paul and Silas were beaten with rods and locked in the inner prison with their feet in stocks.
Around midnight, instead of complaining, they were praying and singing hymns — and the other prisoners were listening.
Suddenly an earthquake shook the prison, all the doors flew open, and everyone’s chains came loose.
thessalonica: Paul went to the Jewish synagogue in Thessalonica, as he usually did, and for three Saturdays in a row he walked people through their own Scriptures.
He showed them the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead — and that Jesus was that Messiah.
Some believed, but others started a riot, and Paul had to escape at night.
patmos: John, the last living apostle, was exiled to the rocky island of Patmos for preaching about Jesus.
One Sunday, while he was worshiping, he heard a loud voice behind him like a trumpet.
He turned and saw the risen Jesus in blazing glory.
Jesus showed him visions of the future, which John wrote down as the Book of Revelation.
new-jerusalem: At the end of the Bible, John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and a holy city coming down from God, beautiful like a bride.
A loud voice says God will live with His people.
He will wipe every tear from their eyes.
There will be no more death, no more sadness, no more crying and no more pain.
